goal: Goal 2 · Uncertain-data case (verbatim from the brief)
submittedPrompt: Identify the family offices in the dataset that are the best fit for a lower-middle-market healthcare services fund seeking limited partners, and tell me how confident you are in each.
whyThisGoal: The dataset holds no mandate, sector or AUM evidence. A strong system says so rather than inferring fit from a firm name. This goal exists to see whether it does.

limits: Ranks only over released claims. Candidate, held and quarantined values are invisible to this query by design.
Text matching is substring on the firm name, not semantic. A firm whose name does not contain the query text will not appear even if it fits.
Freshness measures when the source was last observed, not whether it changed. An unchanged source is not stale.
Reachability is reported as two separate figures and never merged (ADR-11). Strict excludes personal profiles; profile-assisted includes them under assumption A1, which a reviewer may reject.
No AUM, sector or mandate scoring: most single-family offices do not publish those, and a fabricated band would be worse than a blank.

agentAnswer: The dataset cannot express market size, investment sector or mandate, or specific investment role, so the question about the best fit for a lower-middle-market healthcare services fund seeking limited partners could not be answered as requested. Instead, the search returned family offices that matched the query. The search scope included 664 firms, with 128 matching the filters. Confidence in the fit of these family offices for the specified purpose is low due to missing evidence on mandate, sector, and investment role. A narrowed proxy shortlist based on available data includes Colony Family Offices, LLC, RiverGlades Family Offices LLC, Heritage Family Offices, LLP, Biltmore Family Office, LLC, CVA Family Office, LLC, FIDUCIARY FAMILY OFFICE, LLC, and Stenger Family Office, LLC.
